title: 測量学Ⅰ
subtitle: Surveying I
teachers:
NAKANO Kazuya
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: This course covers the fundamental knowledge of surveying, including Surveying Act, public surveying work regulations, and basic surveying principles. Students will learn the principles, equipment, and characteristics of various surveying methods such as observation data processing, distance surveying, and leveling. Spatial information technologies such as GNSS and GIS are introduced here, with detailed study reserved for Surveying II.
advice:
Exercises for each class, solutions to surveyor and assistant surveyor examination questions, and appreciation of "THURUGIDAKE TEN NO KI" correspond to the "Comprehensive Skills" learning component of the CLIP learning process. While surveying methods are diverse, the course progresses by incorporating exercises across a broad spectrum from basic to applied surveying. Furthermore, advanced surveying techniques will be introduced initially, but detailed content will be covered in Surveying II.
1."Overview": History of Surveying Development, Spatial Information Engineering.2."Surveying Act": Surveying-Related Laws, Surveying Act, Standards for Public Surveying Work Regulations, Coordinate Reference Systems. 3."Processing Observed Values": Observed Value Errors, Error Propagation Calculation Methods, Least Squares Method, Processing Observed Values, Calculation Methods for Processing Observed Values, Conversion Between Radians and Degrees. 4."Distance Surveying": Concepts of distance surveying, direct distance measurement, errors in distance surveying. 5."Leveling Surveying": Classification of leveling surveying, definitions of leveling surveying terminology, direct leveling, indirect leveling, types of levels and instruments. 6. Conduct practice exercises for the Assistant Surveyor Examination covering items 1 through 5 above (Relevance to Qualification Certification) , but the schedule may change due to viewing historical documentary films related to surveying. Additionally, a mid-term review test will be administered around the middle of the course. Students who register descriptions related to class management in [Self-Check] may receive extra credit under "Other".)
requiredKnowledge: This course is indispensable for taking Surveying Practice/Seminar I and II and is useful preparation for Spatial Information Engineering. Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II present the lecture contents as a specific application. Spreadsheet software(Excel) can be applied to many survey calculations. Students need to be able to submit reports made using spreadsheets.Additionally, it requires the ability to create Word files for report preparation and a basic level of IT literacy related to this task.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students can explain the Surveying Act and operation specifications for public surveys. They can explain the coordinate reference system accurately, particularly the difference between the world geodetic system and the Japanese geodetic system. Students can handle surveying errors by applying basic mathematical knowledge. They can use the least squares method and process observed values. They can explain the relationship between radians and degrees, and can use Excel to create worksheets. They can also explain the concepts of distance measurement and error, can handle errors, understand and explain the leveling method.
achievementLevels.standard: Students know about the Surveying Act and specifications for public surveys. They can explain the basics of coordinate reference systems. They can also use basic mathematical knowledge and can handle survey errors. Students can  explain the relationship between radians and degrees, the concepts of and errors in distance surveys, leveling, and can outline GNSS, GIS, Remote sensing technology.
